2. The present appellant as plaintiff instituted the aforesaid Money Suit No. 98 of 1988 for realisation of Taka 4,89,230.00 alleging the grounds as stated in the plaint itself. The defendant, namely, Bangladesh Krishi Bank appeared and filed a written statement denying the allegation made in the plaint. Thereafter issues were framed and both the plaintiff and defendant adduced oral as well as documentary evidence and after hearing the arguments of both parties and perusing the materials on record the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit by the judgment holding that since the matter had not been referred to the arbitration as per clause contained in the contract in between the parties, the present suit is not maintainable. 

 3. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellant, submits that the judgment and decree of the trial Court prima facie appears to be illegal and without jurisdiction in view of the provisions of section 34 of the Arbitration Act. Section 34 of the Arbitration Act runs as follows: 

 5. In the present case we find that the plaintiff filed the suit raising several allegations in the plaint. The defendant appeared in the suit and contested the same by filing written statement. Thereafter witnesses of both the parties deposed before the Court and documents have been filed in support of their respective cases. Thereafter in the judgment the learned Subordinate Judge did not consider the suit on its merit on any other issues excepting the issue of maintainability. There is a clause in the contract that if any dispute arises in between the parties with regard to any matter relating to this contract, the matter shall be referred to the Arbitration. From the provisions of law as stated above and from the decisions as referred to above it is found that such an objection must be raised at the very preliminary stage of the proceeding even before taking any step for filing written statement in the suit. If such an objection is not raised at the very preliminary stage and if some steps are taken to file written statement and for doing other necessary steps in the suit, such an application will not be maintainable. Even if at the initial stage such an objection is taken even then the suit will not be dismissed; rather the suit will be kept pending in the Court till the decision in the arbitration proceeding.
